prompt: A city tests two voter-outreach methods. Of $120$ residents who got a door knock, $48$ voted; of $80$ who got a mailer, $28$ voted. Test $H_0: p_1 = p_2$ with the pooled two-proportion $z$-test. What is $z$? Round to two decimal places.
hint: A pooled two-proportion test needs three ingredients: each group's sample proportion and the pooled proportion from both groups combined.

hints.text: A pooled two-proportion test needs three ingredients: each group's sample proportion and the pooled proportion from both groups combined.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: samples of 50 and 50 with 20 and 15 successes: $\hat{p}_c = 35/100 = 0.35$, SE $= \sqrt{0.35 \times 0.65 \times (1/50 + 1/50)} \approx 0.0954$, $z = 0.10/0.0954 \approx 1.05$. Same recipe with unequal sizes.
$\hat{p}_1 = 0.40$, $\hat{p}_2 = 0.35$ and $\hat{p}_c = 76/200 = 0.38$. The standard error is $\sqrt{0.38 \times 0.62 \times (1/120 + 1/80)}$. Divide the difference $0.05$ by it.
The standard error is $\sqrt{0.004908} \approx 0.0701$, so the test statistic is $z = 0.05/0.0701 \approx 0.71$.

explanation: The sample proportions are $\hat{p}_1 = 48/120 = 0.40$ and $\hat{p}_2 = 28/80 = 0.35$, a difference of $0.05$.
Under $H_0$ both methods share one voting rate, so pool the data: $\hat{p}_c = 76/200 = 0.38$.
The sample-size part is $\frac{1}{120} + \frac{1}{80} = 0.02083$, so the standard error is $\sqrt{0.38 \times 0.62 \times 0.02083} = \sqrt{0.004908} \approx 0.0701$.
$z = 0.05/0.0701 \approx 0.71$. The two-sided $p$-value is about $0.48$, so there is no evidence the methods differ.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sanity-check the size of z
steps: A 5-point gap between $40\%$ and $35\%$ sounds real, but each proportion comes from a smallish sample.
The SE of $0.07$ means gaps of 7 points happen routinely by chance; our gap is smaller than that.
So $z$ must be less than 1 — and $0.71$ fits. Always compare the gap to its typical chance size.
